label: prf:archimedean-functor-uniqueness
title: Proof of archimedean realisation uniqueness
html:
Proof sketch

Three ingredients close the conditional statement.

  1. Pentagon-coherence on the substrate. The 5-term pentagon identity is built into the cosimplicial / Yekutieli triple structure of the QOU substrate (cosimplicial crossed groupoid). The motivic class assembled by the mass-formula state sum lives in the Bloch group B(\mathbb{C}) = \mathbb{Z}[\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0,1\}] /\langle\text{5-term pentagon relations}\rangle under this identification.
  2. Bloch-Suslin uniqueness. Suslin [suslin1991] proves that the Suslin map K_3^{\text{ind}}(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R} is unique up to a real scalar; equivalently, any real-valued continuous antisymmetric function on \mathbb{C}\setminus\{0,1\} satisfying the pentagon is a constant scalar multiple of D. This is the K-theoretic incarnation of the rigidity of the Bloch group; see [bloch2000] for the definitive treatment.
  3. Archimedean matching. \tau_{\text{arch}} acting on the substrate's Bloch-group class is, by ingredient 1, a real-valued continuous pentagon-coherent functional on B(\mathbb{C}). By ingredient 2, it is therefore proportional to D. The proportionality constant is fixed by demanding the Faddeev-Kashaev quasi-classical limit (1-q)\log\Phi_n(z;q) \to \mathrm{Li}_2(z) (dilogarithm archimedean limit) match the standard Bloch-Wigner normalisation D(z) = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \log|z|\arg(1-z).
